Scattered rain expected over next 3 days:Ahmedabad records 34.8°C, Rajkot 35.5°C; 5 districts above 35°C
- Copy link
Light rain is likely at isolated places across Gujarat over the next three days. The forecast covers parts of South Gujarat and Saurashtra, including Amreli, Bhavnagar, Surat, Tapi, Navsari, Dang, Valsad, Daman and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. A weather system currently active over the state is expected to bring light rain to these areas.
Temperatures have crossed 35°C in five districts. Ahmedabad recorded 34.8°C, while Rajkot recorded 35.5°C, with residents experiencing hot and humid conditions.
Rainy conditions may continue in parts of Saurashtra and South Gujarat
The Western Disturbance has shifted into a trough, leading to a forecast of light rain over the next three days. No heavy rain is expected anywhere in the state over the next seven days.
The southwest monsoon has almost completely withdrawn from Gujarat. However, some parts of Saurashtra and South Gujarat may continue to experience rainy conditions. The monsoon is also likely to withdraw from the remaining parts of these regions during the day.
Rajkot records 35.5°C as light to moderate rain forecast in parts of Gujarat
According to Meteorological Department Director Dr AK Das, light to moderate rain is likely in parts of Gujarat today and on October 1. Some areas of Saurashtra-Kutch and South Gujarat may receive rainfall during this period.
Ahmedabad is likely to remain cloudy today. The city recorded a maximum temperature of 34.8°C, with residents experiencing hot conditions. Rajkot recorded the highest maximum temperature in the state at 35.5°C.
Winds are expected to blow at speeds of 30–40 kmph along coastal areas today. Fishermen have therefore been advised not to venture into the sea.

Gujarat and its major urban hubs, including Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, and Rajkot, have experienced one of the warmest Octobers in recorded history, anchoring a countrywide heatwave that has pushed back the onset of winter across India.
Data released by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) confirms that October overall proved to be the second-warmest nationally since official record-keeping began in 1901. Driven by persistent atmospheric humidity, a delayed monsoon withdrawal, and a total absence of active Western Disturbances, relentless daytime heat and oppressive nighttime minimums trapped moisture and thermal radiation across Western, Northern, Central, and Southern India.
For Gujarat and the wider Western belt, the extended summer conditions brought prolonged discomfort, leading a broader nation-wide pattern of elevated temperature anomalies.
Gujarat and Western Belt Lead Nationwide 'October Heat'
The Western coastal region and inland plains felt the brunt of high temperatures and severe moisture traps off the Arabian Sea:
Gujarat: Major commercial and administrative centres—including Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Rajkot, and Surat—logged persistent daytime maximums between 36.5°C and 37.8°C (up to 1.6°C above seasonal norms). High relative humidity compounded the thermal stress, keeping nighttime cooling to a minimum across urban pockets.
Maharashtra: Mumbai’s Santacruz observatory recorded daytime peaks reaching 37.6°C, standing a steep 4.5°C above normal. Coastal zones such as Alibaug and Raigad logged averages hovering near 35°C (+2.6°C anomaly).
North-West India Sees Dry Spells and High Night Temperatures
Across the North-Western plains, clear skies and an absence of post-monsoon rain kept afternoon temperatures high while preventing night thermal drop-offs. North-West India recorded its second-warmest October overall, driven by a 76 per cent monthly rainfall deficit:
Delhi-NCR: The primary weather station at Safdarjung registered average daytime maximums of 35.7°C (+1.5°C above normal). Nighttime minimums stayed elevated between 23°C and 24°C—up to 3.4°C above baseline—marking one of the warmest Octobers for the national capital in over seven decades.
Rajasthan: Desert belts including Barmer, Jaisalmer, Pilani, and Churu saw mercury levels regularly breach the 38°C mark, topping out near 39.7°C.
Punjab & Haryana: Agricultural regions surrounding Amritsar, Ludhiana, and Ambala faced prolonged heat spells following a near-total absence of autumn showers.
Central and Southern Peninsula Face Delayed Night Cooling
The delay in cool northerly wind progression extended elevated temperatures across the central and southern states:
Central India: Central India registered its warmest October on record. Key urban centres in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, including Bhopal, Indore, and Raipur, logged minimum night temperatures sitting 2°C to 4°C above baseline, blocking typical post-monsoon evening chill.
South Peninsula: Metropolitan centres such as Hyderabad and Bengaluru registered daytime highs 1.5°C to 3°C above historical monthly benchmarks, pushing South-Peninsula India into its third-warmest October overall.
IMD forecasts indicate that above-normal day and night temperatures will persist across Gujarat and northern India into early November before seasonal winter circulation patterns stabilize.
